rows.why: Item 1 asks how stored values with different case or extra whitespace are read. Its pick trims and lowercases, and the run shows readStatus("  DRAFT ") → 'draft'. So "Draft", " PUBLISHED ", "Merged" and "claimed" would come back as draft, published, merged and claimed.

Item 2 asks which old spellings map to a status. Its pick maps only 'in review' to 'review' and nothing else. 'In-Review' would read as review, but 'under_review' and 'LIVE' would read as null, not review and published as the scenario expects.

Item 3 asks what a value that matches no status returns. Its pick is null and never the nearest status, and the run shows readStatus("drafts") → null. No alias covers closed, archived or revew. Empty and space-only values also read as null (item 7).

Item 5 asks whether writing normalises input or accepts only exact enum values. Its pick accepts exact lowercase enum strings and returns them unchanged: the run shows writeStatus("draft") → 'draft'. So writing "review" stores "review".

Item 5 is about refusing anything but exact enum values on write. The run shows 'Draft', ' draft' and 'in-review' all throw, so old spellings are refused on write. Item 6 confirms the error message names the value as given, JSON-quoted (e.g. 'not a sandbox status: " Draft"').

Item 8 asks how a batch read reports unreadable values. Its pick keeps every row, sets unreadable ones to null, and lists each distinct raw value once, sorted. The runs for items 8 and 9 show raw values kept as stored, e.g. ' Bogus ' and 'BOGUS'.
